headline: Approved Michelle Bettencourt as secretary and James Eric Rogers as treasurer, and accepted a 2026-2027 workplan.
summary: The director reported on Medicare enrollment help, staffing changes, and a $4,000 national grant for a community garden. Discussion covered senior housing projects, a kitchen renovation with no completion date, and resident and visitor parking passes.
decisions: Approved appointing Michelle Bettencourt as Secretary, James Eric Rogers as Treasurer, and John Russell as Vice-Chair by unanimous roll call vote.
Accepted the Annual Report and draft 2026-2027 workplan by unanimous roll call vote.
Approved the September 16, 2026 regular meeting minutes by unanimous roll call vote.

SALEM COUNCIL ON AGING  
ANNUAL MEETING MINUTES 
 
Date and Time:  October 21, 2026 at 5:15 P.M.  
Meeting Location:  VIA ZOOM  
Members Present:  Lynda Coffill (LC, Chair), John Russell (JR, Vice-Chair), Kristin 
Macek (KM, Secretary), George Barbuzzi (GB), Michelle 
Bettencourt (MB), and James Eric Rogers (JER)  
Absent: Eliud Alcala (EA), Abigail Butt (AB, Treasurer) and Patricia Small 
(PS) 
Also Present:  Teresa Arnold, (TA, Director of the COA) and Clerk Joanne M. 
Roomey 
 
I. MEETING CALLED TO ORDER 
LC called the meeting to order at 5:15 p.m.  
 
II. CHAIRPERSON’S REPORT:  
      Review of the past year 
LC presented the Board with the Annual Report of the Chairperson: 
I am honored to be the chairperson of the Board. What a pleasure it is to work with 
such a wonderful group of Board members! Their dedication and willingness to 
advocate fiercely for our senior citizens is remarkable and very much appreciated. 
These folks chair committees, and work to make sure the tasks of the committees are 
done. For example, for the past few years, members have planted gardens in raised beds 
at the center. They grow herbs and vegetables for our seniors. Other members bring 
ideas to the Board for programs to benefit our constituency. Thank you to all of you.  
It is also a blessing to work with the Director of the Council on Aging and Senior 
Services. Teresa Arnold is the epitome of professionalism. Her diligence and dedication 
are apparent in all that she does. This year due to the loss of half of position, Ms. Arnold 
has had to assume more responsibilities. She has done so efficiently without complaint. 
The staff of the Council on Aging includes two licensed Social Workers, a Social 
Service Navigator, an Activities Coordinator, a Transportation Coordinator, van  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
DOMINICK PANGALLO                 
MAYOR 
 
 
CITY OF SALEM, MASSACHUSETTS 
COUNCIL ON AGING BOARD & 
SENIOR SERVICES BOARD 
401 BRIDGE STREET  
SALEM, MA  01970 
TEL: 978-744-0924 
 
 
 
 
 
 
LYNDA COFFILL, CHAIR 
JOHN RUSSELL, VICE CHAIR 
 
    TERESA GOVE ARNOLD 
 DIRECTOR
2 
 
drivers, a Dining Services Coordinator, an hourly Memory Café Coordinator and a part-
time Fiscal Clerk. These individuals are to be admired for their hard work and 
persistence in times of stress and lack of resources. 
The officers of the Board are John Russell, Vice Chairperson, Dr. Abigail Butt, 
Treasurer and Kristen Macek, Secretary. Although we do not have money of our own, 
Dr. Butt reviews the budget with the Director. Ms. Macek can be called on when 
needed. John Ru ssell is my right -hand man. His contributions to the Board are 
numerous. He is the liaison between the Board and the Friends of the Council on Aging. 
He and his crew prepare the food for our celebratory cookouts. 
Mr. Russell uses the Community Life Center parking lot during Haunted Happenings 
to raise funds for both the Friends and the Park and Recreation department. He has also 
been a valuable advisor on the kitchen project. Thank you to all of you. Your 
willingness to pitch in when needed is much appreciated. 
The following is a summary of our workplace progress during the year. 
Continue monitoring the Director of the Council on Aging on activities, budget 
and services. Ms. Arnold reports to the Board at every meeting. She brings issues and 
progress on projects to the attention of the Board. Between meetings, she is quick to 
inform the Chairperson of any issues that may need advocacy and action by the Board. 
These issues are brought up at the meetings, discussed and, if needed, a plan of action 
developed. With a full social service team finally in place, Ms. Arnold continued to 
provide supervision and support. Programs and activities were sponsored and or 
participated in b y members of the Board. Members supported the community by 
walking in the Haunted Happenings and in the Salem 400+ Parades in costume! 
Another of our contributions to Salem 400+ was the sponsoring of two lectures, 
facilitated by Ms. Arnold, by Jim McAllister about the contributions of Salem Seniors 
through the ages. Both lectures were well attended, and attendees were very positive 
about them. 
Continue Monitoring the redesign of the kitchen and other building needs. The 
need to create a commercial kitchen has been at the forefront of Board advocacy for 
years. This year, the kitchen is in the process of being renovated and should be 
operational by Christmas. Thanks to Ms. Arnold for her dogged determination to see 
this project through. Thanks also to Mr. Russell for his continued participation on the 
advisory board for this. 
Our Dining Services Coordinator resigned in August. Since then, Ms. Arnold has been 
working to identify and supply the needed staff for the meals program. Hopefully, this 
will be resolved before the kitchen work is completed. 
Continue to advocate for an appropriate salary for the director and staff and 
advocate for the half-time position to be reinstated. This issue remains unresolved. 
We will continue advocacy on this. 
Advocate for and monitor the development of new senior housing units. This 
year we witnessed the opening of senior units developed by the North Shore 
Community Development Corporation. The Lee Fort Terrace project was also 
completed and seniors have moved in. Of the original fifty -one residents of Lee Fort
3 
 
Terrace who were rehoused during the construction, twelve opted not to move back. 
Board members toured these properties which add safe, secure and modern housing for 
our seniors. Our advocacy on these projects contributed to their fruition. 
 Continue support for the Friends of the Council on Aging. This group of hard 
working and dedicated volunteers make many of the programs and activities happen.  
Without their support, the COA would be less welcoming, fun and active. Members of 
the Board have continued supporting their fundraising programs and will continue to 
do so in the future. 
 Plan and Implement a Senior Day to recognize and honor the contribution 
senior citizens make to the life of the city. On August 5th, the third annual Salem 
Senior Celebration was held at Winter Island. The committee was co-chaired by George 
Barbuzzi from the Board and Beth Debski from the Friends. This day was a huge  
success with two hundred seniors in attendance. Three seniors were honored, Martha 
Bagby, Elwena Tungol and Luisa Espinal. The food was grilled by Mr. Russell and his 
faithful crew and was added to by John Harvey. Mr. Harvey’s contributions were 
culinary, financial and physical. Thanks to these wonderful men, everyone had a great 
lunch. Also, thanks to all the volunteers who made the day a delight. One would be 
remiss if Rosanna Donahue was not recognized. Her tireless efforts both in the planning 
and on the day of the event were admirable. 
 Explore ways to improve participant diversity in COA activities, programs, 
and services. This is one area that the Board has not made any progress. However, 
progress has been made with the staff addition of a bilingual Social Service Navigator 
who conducts outreach. Our staff person, accompanied by a staff person from the 
Mayor’s office, canvas neighborhoods to inform citizens of the services and activities 
offered by the city and the COA. 
 Continue collaborations with Salem for All Ages including co -sponsoring 
events. It appears that Salem for All Ages is not active. Therefore, this activity could 
not be fulfilled. 
The year has passed and we move on with renewed energy and enthusiasm for the year 
to come. 
III. ELECTION OF OFFICERS:   
      Election of Officers 
KM made a motion to appoint the following: Michelle Bettencourt as Secretary , James Eric 
Rogers as Treasurer and to accept the prior appointment of John Russell as Vice-Chair.  
LC asked for other nominations from the floor. Hearing none, she asked KM to cast a vote for 
the slate. JER seconded the motion. 
 
KM closed the nominations. Seconded by JR. A roll call vote was taken, and the motion was 
carried unanimously. The Chair, Lynda Coffill, was previously appointed by the mayor for 
another two-year term.
4 
 
 
IV. REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF WORKPLAN FOR 2026-2027 
LC presented the Annual Report of the Chairperson and a Workplan for 2026 - 2027 and asked 
if there were any additions or deletions. LC suggested allowing one month to review the plan 
and determine whether any items should be added or removed. The plan includes the following: 
• Continue monitoring COA Activities, budgets, programs and services 
 
• Continue advocacy for appropriate salary for Director and all staff 
 
• Continue advocacy to reinstate lost position 
 
• Continue advocacy for increases in senior housing programs 
 
• Continue support for the Friends of the Salem Council on Aging 
 
• Continue the annual Senior Celebration 
 
JR made a motion to accept the Annual Report and Draft Workplan and motion was seconded 
by JER. A roll call vote was taken, and the motion was carried unanimously.  
IV. VOTE TO ADJOURN 
There being no further business to come before the Council on Aging & Senior Services 
Board this evening; JR moved to adjourn the meeting. Seconded by KM. A roll call vote was 
taken, and the motion was carried unanimously. The meeting was adjourned at 5:20 p.m.  
Respectfully Submitted,  
 
 
 
Joanne M. Roomey 
Board Clerk

SALEM COUNCIL ON AGING & SENIOR SERVICES 
REGULAR MONTHLY MEETING MINUTES 
 
Date and Time:  October 21, 2026 at 5:30 p.m.  
Meeting Location:  Levesque Community Life Center Conference Room 
401 Bridge Street, Salem, MA 
 
Members Present:  Lynda Coffill (LC, Chair), John Russell (JR, Vice-Chair), Kristin 
Macek (KM, Secretary), George Barbuzzi (GB), Michelle 
Bettencourt (MB), and James Eric Rogers (JER)  
Absent: Eliud Alcala (EA), Abigail Butt (AB, Treasurer) and Patricia Small 
(PS) 
Also Present:  Teresa Arnold, (TA, Director of the COA & Senior Services); and 
Clerk Joanne M. Roomey 
 
I. MEETING CALLED TO ORDER  
LC called the meeting to order at 5:21 p.m.  
II. APPROVAL OF THE SEPTEMBER 16, 2026 REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  
A motion was made by JR to approve the September 16, 2026, Regular Meeting Minutes. 
Seconded by KM. A roll call vote was taken, and the motion was carried unanimously.    
III. DIRECTOR’S REPORT 
Social Services: 
• Open enrollment for Medicare plans has begun. Many changes are occurring in 2027 
especially with Medicare Advantage plans leaving folks very confused and 
overwhelmed. 
• Three Shine volunteers who take a total of nine appointments per week are already 
booked; Sharon is booked and Fabiola has some slots still open. The Regional SHINE 
office is also fully booked so once Fabiola is booked, we will need to refer folks to 
Medicare’s 1-800# like last year. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
DOMINICK PANGALLO                 
MAYOR 
 
 
CITY OF SALEM, MASSACHUSETTS 
COUNCIL ON AGING & 
SENIOR SERVICES BOARD 
401 BRIDGE STREET  
SALEM, MA  01970 
TEL: 9787440924 
 
 
 
 
 
 
LYNDA COFFILL, CHAIR 
JOHN RUSSELL, VICE CHAIR 
 
    TERESA GOVE ARNOLD 
 DIRECTOR
2 
 
• Staffing: Ingrid Patterson has accepted a job with the City Clerk’s office. She is 
splitting her time this and next week and will be full -time in the Clerk’s office on 
November 2. TA has a meeting with the mayor tomorrow and is requesting that we go 
back to the former staffing model of three social workers. The Board advocated for the 
third position a few years ago. We had a challenging time filling the position so hired 
Ms. Patterson as a Social Service Navigator who conducted outreach as well. Fabiola 
Alvarez speaks Spanish, so we have that skill in the department which should allow us 
to hire a social worker (or similar degree) to meet the demands. 
• Fuel and Property tax exemption forms are being completed by the team. However, 
with Ingrid transferring to the City Clerk’s office, we will have to delay appointments 
until after Open Enrollment for these forms or inform folks they can go directly to 
North Shore Community Action Programs for fuel assistance and the Assessor’s office 
for property tax exemption assistance. Sharon has already informed Claudia  Forgione 
in the Assessor’s office who handles the property tax exemption forms. 
• Housing updates: The approximate wait for a Salem resident to be offered a unit in 
subsidized housing is 2.5-3 years leaving so many very vulnerable. Sometimes we can 
help people obtain emergency status i.e. no -fault eviction or severe medical 
emergencies. These emergency situations or Veterans seem to be approximately a 6-9 
month wait (sometime sooner). 
• Statistics: Last month 300 individuals were serviced 522 times with these issues plus 
other i.e., SNAP, home care options, Social Security issues and retirement questions. 
Activities/Programs: 
• Our participation in the Haunted Happenings Parade was a hit with Alice in  
Wonderland as our theme. Thanks to Board members, staff and seniors who 
participated. 
• A group of seniors traveled to the Topsfield Fair on Monday, October 5. 
• Careforth Adult Foster Care sponsored a Trunk or Treat event in the parking lot on 
Wednesday, October 14 for the seniors. 
• On Monday, October 26, there will be a field trip to the Maple Street Bistro at Essex 
Tech. 
• On Tuesday, October 27, the Delvena Theatre Company will present Mangia, 
Meatballs and Murder. 
• The annual Halloween party luncheon will be on Thursday, October 29. 
Transportation:
3 
 
• In September, 86 passengers were provided with 964 one-way rides. 
• Two drivers who were out for a period are back and we are better staffed but advertising 
for a part-time driver to fill in for some gaps. 
Dining Services/Kitchen Update: 
• There was no response to the Request for Proposal. While one organization was 
interested, they presently do not have the bandwidth to support our request but would 
be interested in the future. 
• Suzanne Harrigan, who is our temporary part -time Dining Services Coordinator, is 
willing to increase to 30 hours a week once the kitchen is complete. At that point, we 
will resume full luncheon operations and begin some schedule of a la carte self -cook 
luncheon alternatives. 
Memory Café/Reiki Clinic: 
• The monthly Reiki Clinic was held on October 8. 
• There is no Memory Café this month due to the last Thursday of the month being so 
close to Halloween. 
• September’s Memory Café was a hit with the visit from the Lazy J Ranch therapeutic 
mini horses. 
Other: 
• In collaboration with the Health Department, we hosted a Flu Clinic on October 7. 
• The second rotation of Salem State nursing students started today. Students and their 
professor, Dr. Barbara Poremba, visit once a week for six-week rotations. We have two 
groups; one Wednesdays and one on Thursdays for the academic year. Students offer 
blood pressure checks and health and nutrition education. 
• The COA and the Veteran’s Department will cohost an event on Tuesday, 
November 10 to present the story of Salemite Nelson “Sparky” Nersasian who was one 
of the 28 men to survive the torpedoing and sinking of destroyer USS Leopold in 1944. 
Col. Bob Nersasian, who wrote the book Never to Return, will be with us. 
• Looking ahead, we will hold our annual Remembrance Ceremony on Tuesday, 
November 17. 
• The Residence at Vinnin Square will sponsor a Thanksgiving luncheon for our 
participants on Thursday, November 19.
4 
 
• Great news is that we will be awarded $4,000 for a Cultivating Connected 
Communities Prize Challenge grant .  The Administration for Community Living 
(ACL) conducted a Cultivating Connected Communities Prize Challenge, a national 
competition that supports community garden projects working to expand accessibility, 
healthy eating, and community connection for people with disabilities and older adults. 
Potential activities may include accessibility upgrades, adaptive gardening tools, and 
inclusive programming enhancements that help reduce social isolation, support well -
being, and improve access to fresh foods. Spec ial thanks to Kerry Murphy from the 
Health Dept. who wrote the application with information supplied by JER and TA. 
• LC had a question regarding Ingrid Patterson working with seniors regarding Housing. 
Lori Stewart was out on medical and Ingrid filled in for her  at City Hall. L C had a 
concern/opinion regarding teaming an outreach worker with the mayor’s office ; may 
or may not be a good idea. She’s not sure that the return on that was worth it. TA will 
discuss with the mayor.  
IV. OLD BUSINESS:  
a. Senior Housing:  
LC read a couple of weeks ago the Salem State University south campus senior housing 
project is going forward. LC said they were going to do the large unit first, but they are 
moving forward on the senior piece. She thinks it is necessary for us to be aware where 
they are in the process and how many affordable units there will be. Apparently, there 
are 110 senior units as part of the plan. We need to stay on top of this.  LC will contact 
Lori Stewart to see what information she might have. 
 
Winn Development will be building on the crescent lot near the train station, and it 
should be finished in 2028. LC thinks it is all market rate. MB thinks there is an 
affordable program at the Cresent Lot , not just for seniors. LC understands that 
underground parking is going under the former Essex County Building on Federal 
Street. Ten units will be developed there. The only thing for seniors is the SSU campus. 
until the CDC development, El Centro, begins and finishes. 
 
b. CLC Kitchen: 
TA emailed Facilities Director Michael Crounse for an update. The plumber was onsite 
today to do grease traps. We are waiting on the HVAC subcontractor regarding the AC 
unit. It has been a slow install and held up for a variety of reasons The city only has a 
couple of inspectors available. Mike Crounse will keep us apprised. There is no date of 
completion announced. 
.  
c. RESIDENT AND VISITOR PARKING PASSES
5 
 
LC reached out to the mayor but has not received any response to the email. Brendon 
Walsh already wrote his concerns in the newspaper a while  ago. LC will make one 
more attempt to contact the mayor. Then, she will write a letter to the editor if there is 
no response as to how this is impacting seniors. TA recommended chatting with 
Councilor King as well.  
 
d. REBRANDING 
TA said Abby introduced her to Ansa Stamper, who helped with the Lincoln COA & 
Human Services rebranding, and they will get together the second week of 
November.  
e. WOMEN’S EXPO 2027 
MB reported that the  committee met and solidified a flyer to promote the event.  JER 
has contacted Gulu for the beer and wine. He will follow up in November. Flying 
Saucer will provide pizza. Botanical is going to do a sugar scrub. Other store owners 
will be invited to participate. The next Expo meeting is on November 10 at the CLC. 
 
V. NEW BUSINESS:   
a. Friends of the COA Report  
JR reported that the Friends no longer meet monthly. 
Currently, the parking lot earnings for the Halloween season are at $4,000. JR is 
hopeful that we will make more money this weekend and it could help that Halloween 
is on a Saturday. People come back every year to the CLC lot because they know 
where the money is going. 
 Beth Debski is moving to Florida, so she will be leaving the board. JR said that she is 
going to be hard to replace. LC mentioned that one of her friends retired in July who 
may be a great fit for the Friends. John Harvey is now on the Friends Board
6 
 
VI. OTHER BUSINESS:  
      EVENT SPONSORED BY SALEM ROTARY 
TA mentioned that the Rotary event, Back to the 1970’s is rescheduled for Thursday, 
November 12 from 4:00-7:00 pm. 
VII. NEXT REGULAR BOARD MEETING: Wednesday, November 18, 2026. 
VIII. VOTE TO ADJOURN 
There being no further business to come before the COA & Senior Services Board this 
evening; JR moved to adjourn the meeting. Seconded by JER. A roll call vote was taken, 
and the motion was carried unanimously. The meeting adjourned at 5:55 p.m.  
Respectfully Submitted, 
  
 
Joanne M. Roomey 
Board Clerk 
 
Know Your Rights under the Open Meeting Law M.G.L. Chapter 30A ss. 1825 and City Ordinance  
Sections 22028 through 22033.
